name: kelmar
author: weather-and-seasons designer
description:
kelmar (direction: weather and seasons) -- RAIN SHOWERS OVER A GARDEN ROW: THE PLANTS
STANDING JUST OUTSIDE THE RAIN. PRIVATE; never shown to players.

CLUE = "<ground>/*<a>Y<b>". <ground> is one row of bare earth "_" 42-52 columns wide with
5-8 flowers "*" and 4-7 small trees "Y" planted on it, never closer than 3 columns apart
and never in the outermost two columns. a and b are 1..3 with a+b<=5, a <= flowers-3 and
b <= trees-3 (so a digit is never the number of plants of that kind, and there are always
spare plants of both kinds). The glyph is written next to its digit, so which digit belongs
to which plant is never a gratuitous ambiguity.

SOLUTION = a picture of rain falling on that garden. The scorer drops blank lines,
right-strips, and requires the LAST line to be the clue's ground row verbatim. Every line
above it is a sky row: "#", "|", "/" and "'" all read as rain, space, "." and "_" as dry
sky, anything else is rejected. There must be at least two sky rows and they must all be
IDENTICAL (the rain falls straight down), each as long as the ground row. Every maximal run
of rain (a "shower") must be at least 3 columns wide, consecutive showers must be separated
by at least 2 dry columns, and there must be at least 2 showers. Sky height (2-4), which
rain glyph, dots or spaces for dry sky, indentation and blank lines are all free.

THE RULE: exactly a FLOWERS and exactly b TREES stand in the column immediately to the left
or immediately to the right of a shower -- dry, right at the edge of the rain, just missing
it. Wet plants never count; plants two or more columns clear never count. Nothing else is
checked: which plants they are, how many showers there are, how wide they are and how much
of the garden gets rained on are all free.

INTENDED PATH: one demo gives the whole grammar (the clue is the bottom line); the only
question is what the two digits count. Rounds 2-3 go on "how many got rained on", "how many
stayed dry", "how many showers", "how many showers have a plant under them" and the near
miss "the plant under the last drop" -- every shipped demo falsifies all of them -- and the
crack is the sentence a 12-year-old says while pointing: "that one is standing right on the
edge of the shower and staying dry".

DEGENERATE WITNESSES CLOSED (400 fresh clues; every attacker knows the grammar perfectly
and builds a legal picture satisfying its own hypothesis, 500 tries per clue): random legal
picture 6-8 %, best blind sampler over 15 density settings 13.2 %, sampler matched to the
demos' own shower-count/width/gap distribution 10.0 %, "rain on a of them / b of them" (the
natural first probe) 6.2 %, "a of them stay dry" 4.5 %, "at the last WET column" (the
nose-vs-tail near miss) 7.0 %, "beside rain, wet or dry" 1-2 %, "two columns clear" 5.2 %,
"within two columns" 16.2 %, "showers with one under them" 4.5-8.0 %, solid rain with 2-wide
holes at the first a+b plants 16.2 % (the best insight-free template), one big shower 4.0 %,
regular stripes 7.8 %, rain over the first a+b plants 0.0 %, one fixed picture for every
clue 7.0 %, previous clue's answer 0.0 %, the previous demo's sky grafted onto this clue
9.2 %, junk/empty/clue echoed 0.0 %. The readings that DO pay are all the intended insight
in weaker forms: one side of the relation only 27.5/33.2 %, the relation applied carelessly
30.2 %, the relation without telling flowers from trees 39-46 %, the relation counted per
shower instead of per plant 84.8 %, the rule 100 %.

FAIRNESS FLOOR: of 34 hand-built "count a relation in this picture" laws, 2-5 survive one
demo, 1-2 survive two, and the last survivor is the true rule in 6/6 trials.

solve() picks a target plants and b trees, hangs showers so that exactly those stand at an
edge, protects one spare flower and one spare tree from any rain, then hill-climbs on decoy
showers until every rival statistic above differs from the clue's digits AND the picture
also shows: a plant on a shower's last wet column, a plant two columns clear of the rain, a
plant deep inside a shower, a plant far from any rain, and a shower that catches nobody.
83 % of demos meet all of that; the rest miss exactly one item. Layout, rain glyph, dry
glyph, sky height and shower count all vary between demos, so no demo is a template for the
next. Design notes and the full witness table: challenges/lab/NOTES_weather.md.
score:
def score(c,s):
 g,k=c.split("/");W=len(g)
 L=[x.rstrip()for x in s.split("\n")if x.strip()]
 if len(L)<3 or L[-1]!=g:return 0
 P={re.sub("[#|/']","1",re.sub("[ ._]","0",x.ljust(W)))for x in L[:-1]}
 p=P.pop()
 if P or len(p)!=W or set(p)-set("01"):return 0
 R=[m.span()for m in re.finditer("1+",p)]
 if len(R)<2 or any(b-a<3 or(i and a-R[i-1][1]<2)for i,(a,b)in enumerate(R)):return 0
 E=[g[i]for a,b in R for i in(a-1,b)if 0<=i<W]
 return int(E.count("*")==int(k[1])and E.count("Y")==int(k[3]))
